Columns of the grid and rows under Channels, in order. Any of "desktop", "email", "push" and "slack".

Desktop reads the browser's permission. When it hasn't been asked, Allow asks; when it's blocked, it says where to change it; when the browser can't show notifications, it says so. Slack starts disconnected: its column is off, and Connect opens a dialog to pick a workspace and channel. If connecting fails, the reason shows in the dialog and nothing is lost.
Disconnect Slack after the person confirms.
Dismisses a test notification banner while it has focus.

Each channel has a Send test that really sends. Desktop and push show a notification banner over the page, and desktop also fires a real system notification once the browser allows it. Email opens a preview of the message in an inbox, the digest version when emails are bundled. Slack shows the message as your team sees it in the channel.

Every AI product ends up with the same notifications page: a list of things that can happen, a list of places they can reach you, and a way to make it stop at night. NotificationSettings is that page as one section. It drops into a SettingsSection and uses the same draft, save bar and unsaved-changes guard as the rest of Settings.
In the grid, jump to the start or end of the row. With Ctrl or ⌘, to the first or last checkbox.
In the grid, move between checkboxes. Left and right follow reading direction.
Moves into the grid once, to the last checkbox you used, then on to the channels.
Must be inside a SettingsSection.

On phones every channel chip is a 44px target.

Pass events to add or drop rows and channels to pick columns. Each event can carry a sample for test previews and urgent to let it through quiet hours. onSlackConnect gets the chosen workspace and channel; throw to show why it failed, and the dialog stays open.

Pass the saved preferences and an async onSave. Edits stay in a draft until someone saves from the save bar or with ⌘S. Return field errors to show them under the field, or throw to show the message in the save bar. onSendTest sends a real test before the preview appears.

Quiet hours hold desktop and push alerts between two times on the days you pick, in the time zone you pick, with a line that says when the next quiet period starts or that it's quiet now. Urgent events like approvals can still come through.
Row, column and corner checkboxes are mixed when only some are on, so screen readers hear "partially checked".
Rows of the grid: { id, label, description?, urgent?, sample? }. sample is { title, body, subject, action } for test previews. urgent events can come through quiet hours.
Save the draft. Return { quietDays: "…" } and the like to show field errors, or throw to show the message in the save bar.
Send a real test. The preview shows once it resolves, and the button offers a retry if it throws. event is the first one that's on for that channel.
Test banners pause while hovered or focused, have a dismiss button, and fade instead of sliding with reduced motion.
Test sends, permission results and Slack changes are announced politely. The next quiet period is a status line that updates as you edit.
The connected Slack channel. While it's null, the Slack column is off.

The core is a grid of events by channels. The top row turns a channel on or off for every event, the first column turns an event on or off everywhere, and the corner checkbox does all of it. Each shows a dash when only some are on. With the keyboard the grid is one tab stop: arrow keys move between checkboxes, Home and End jump along a row, and Space toggles. Screen readers hear each one as "Email for Agent finished". On a phone the grid becomes one card per event with large channel chips.
The default channels: desktop, email, push and slack.
The default events: Agent finished, Needs approval, Run failed, Mentions, Weekly summary and Billing.
The grid is an ARIA grid with column and row headers, and every checkbox is named by its channel and event, like "Mobile push for Run failed".
The phone that gets push notifications.
The whole section: the event grid, channels with tests, quiet hours and the email digest.
Turns the focused checkbox on or off. On a row, column or corner checkbox, turns all of them on, or off when all are on.

What's saved now: { matrix, quietHours, quietFrom, quietTo, quietDays, timeZone, quietUrgent, digest }. matrix maps each event id to the channels that are on. When it changes and there are no edits, the draft follows it.
